$comment: Serialisable Jev question set for the criterion-strength lens (PLAT-837). Verbatim from the ticket: ids, question text, enum members and rubric levels are transcribed, not paraphrased, so the later API-integration task can hand this document to the Jev client unchanged. One request per FR, one question block per AC row, per PLAT-837's 'Question set' section.
request_shape: One request per FR, one question block per AC row. State: the FR statement, the AC row, the FR's Description/Behaviour/Constraints.

noul.question: Is there a concrete system behaviour that would make this criterion false?
Does it name something observable from outside, rather than a property of the implementation?
If it asserts a quantity, is the number actually stated?
Is this the FR sentence with `shall` swapped out?
Does it name an internal symbol, private field, or call sequence?
noul.note: The subtle one: an AC naming an internal function is satisfiable by exactly one implementation and passes forever after it is written. That is over-specification, a distinct defect from vagueness, and it is why ACs survive refactors that should have broken them.

choice.question: Classify this acceptance criterion's weakness, if any.

score.scope: per FR (aggregate over the FR's AC set), not per AC row
score.scope_provenance: derived, not verbatim ticket text. PLAT-837 states adverse_case_coverage as a `score` without spelling out its aggregation unit in so many words; this field is this skill's inference from the rubric's own shape (a single AC row cannot by itself carry 'happy + errors + edge + negative case' — that vocabulary only makes sense read across an FR's whole AC set) and from PLAT-837's Question set section, which states one Jev request per FR (not per AC row) for this dimension. Kept in its own field, explicitly marked derived, rather than folded into the `noul`/`choice` items PLAT-837 does state verbatim, per PR #570 review.

rubric.label: happy + errors + edge + explicit negative case

score.note: `specify` already instructs authors to cover happy/error/edge and negative cases. Nothing currently measures whether they complied. This rubric makes that instruction countable.

authority.note: Findings only. This lens never edits an AC, never authors a requirement, never changes a matrix row. Its only write is the SpecReview artifact.
authority.low_confidence: annotated, not suppressed — the finding still appears in the table marked unconfirmed.
